Timed Word Tile Rush vs untimed Word Search

Compare current Word Tile Rush’s 90-second, per-letter scoring with Word Search’s untimed eight-by-eight endpoint-selection puzzle; neither saves a game record.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Check the current platform.

Use the public pages behind this explanation.

Open the ArcadeReview PrivacyKeyboard-only play notes

Bottom line: Word Tile Rush is a timed word-path game; Word Search is an untimed straight-line hunt. Their boards, scoring, and controls differ, and neither stores a best score or progress record in current V2.

Current rules side by side

FeatureWord Tile RushWord Search
Board6×8 rising letter grid8×8 letter grid
PathTrace adjacent letters, including diagonals; do not reuse a tileSelect the first and last letters of a straight horizontal, vertical, or diagonal word
Clock90 seconds after the first tile selectionNo countdown
Score or progressOne point per letter in each accepted wordFound-word count out of four
RecordCurrent run onlyCurrent puzzle only

Word Tile Rush: clear before time runs out

A valid word is checked against a small built-in list. Its letters disappear, the remaining letters settle within their columns, and a new row enters at the bottom. The run ends at zero seconds or when the top row becomes occupied after an accepted word.

Word Search: choose endpoints

Word Search lists four words. Select the first and last cells of a straight line; lines may run in either direction horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. The board counts found words, and the puzzle completes when all four have been found. There is no countdown or speed bonus.

Controls and storage boundaries

Both games use labeled cell buttons and standard controls that can be reached with the keyboard. Word Search also offers row and column selectors for choosing an endpoint; Word Tile Rush provides Submit word and Clear path. Exact keyboard behavior is on each live game page.

The displayed score or found-word count belongs to the current page session. NoCharge V2 does not save a local best, solved count, or last-list record for these games. Neither game is presented as vocabulary training or a measure of attention.
